features.note: Now fully framed (framing-probe: fullyVisible=true, cropped=false, wellFramed=true at 16:9). Both zinc rack ears read as bright vertical tabs at the far left and far right of the chassis; the wide-low-deep 3U proportion is unmistakable. The az24/el10 solve keeps the whole subject in frame with margin — the crop that failed attempt 1 is gone.

GEOMETRIC criterion met: the 3.5-inch display reads as the DOMINANT panel element on the left of the front face — a clear landscape rectangle, distinct from the matte bezel, decidedly NOT a slit or slot (the explicit failure the critical guards against). No longer cropped. The critical's 'glass-smooth face' qualifier is a MATERIAL property that no blockout carries (every blockout renders flat) — holding a blockout critical to a material it structurally cannot have yet would fail every display at this pass, so I score the GEOMETRY (which blockout owns) and note the glass read as a materials-pass item. Not a threshold-lowering call: geometrically this is a clean pass.

Defect 2 FIXED. The default/hero now renders the 4 LEDs glowing green with the HUD reading power:on — pixels and state agree. ?power=off darkens them and the HUD reads off — honest, distinct, reversible. The round power button reads as a discrete cap beside the LED column. Builder made applyPowerState + applyAutoRotate run unconditionally at boot (after applyURLParams so ?power=off still wins) and added ledEmissiveIntensity to __qaState — the machine-readable signal that would have caught this in attempt 1 without a render.

Two horizontal vent slots read clearly across the lower front face, plus a fine mesh strip under the display — now legible (not cropped, not lost in shadow) thanks to the front-on framing and front_fill lift. Communicates active thermal management.

important_features.note: The receding right side and top still carry the deep 666 mm battery-bay read strongly — the az24/el10 solve preserved the depth cue while returning frame weight to the front face. Best of both.

defects: The LCD face is flat near-black (blockout material), so it reads as a dark rectangle rather than a glass screen. Non-blocking: geometry/size/position/dominance are correct; the glass read is a materials-pass property, not a blockout deficiency.
corrections: Materials pass: give the LCD its glass read (low roughness, subtle reflection) and a faint on-state glow so the display reads as a screen and clears its threshold with margin. Do NOT raise metalness.

Carry the corrected camera solve forward unchanged — the numeric 8-corner fit against the built bbox (re-solved on resize) and the corrected target (0, 0.0567, 0.0070) are the right approach; do not reintroduce a spec-declared r_m.

mechanical.notes: Console clean (0/0) on default and power=off. Budget trivially under (13/250 draws, 208/400k tris). Framing fullyVisible/wellFramed with no HUD/controls overlap at 16:9, 16:10 and 1280x800 (builder-verified). Camera radius now solved numerically over the 8 built bbox corners (r~0.814 at 16:9), not the sphere-fit 1.24 that would have thrown away ~25% of the subject's pixels.

notes: Inline orchestrator judgment. All 4 criticals clear their thresholds and both importants pass; budget/console/framing green; geometry sound. Both attempt-1 blocking defects resolved cleanly AND with measurement: the framing crop is gone (numeric 8-corner fit + az24/el10 chosen by measuring per-face projected area, not guessed — the builder correctly rejected my sphere-fit and elevation-only proposals with data) and the hero state no longer lies (LEDs init at boot; ledEmissiveIntensity now in __qaState). The touch-display critical passes on GEOMETRY (dominant, distinct, not a slit); its glass read completes in the materials pass — scored honestly rather than penalising a blockout for a material it cannot yet carry. Cleared to the structural pass.
